sources.description: journalctl serializes journal entries to JSON; strings, arrays, byte arrays and null have distinct meanings.
sources.location: Binary .journal files under /run/log/journal or /var/log/journal; journalctl -o json provides a textual export.
sources.collection: Check journald storage policy, namespace, rate limiting and access. Export selected authorized entries with journalctl -o json.
uses: Test parsers against scalar strings, repeated fields, binary arrays and null values.
For real events, correlate _BOOT_ID, process identifiers and timestamps; these metadata fields are absent from this format-demonstration sample.
sources.limitations: This is the publisher’s serialization demonstration, not a captured security event. JSON is not the binary journal file format.

field_notes._UDEV_DEVLINK: Repeated values become a JSON array.
field_notes.BINARY: Non-text bytes become a numeric array.
field_notes.LARGE: null can represent a field omitted because of its size.

sources.title: osquery differential results
sources.description: Scheduled query differential results describe rows added or removed relative to the query’s prior state.
sources.location: Configured logger destination, commonly osqueryd.results.log; not the INFO status log.
sources.collection: Review the scheduled SQL, interval, host identifier and differential versus snapshot mode.
uses: Investigate a new process or configuration row with its query name and schedule.
Keep removed and added results together when evaluating state changes.
sources.limitations: A scheduled process-table query can miss short-lived processes. An added row is a state delta, not automatically a real-time creation event.

field_notes.action: added, removed or snapshot semantics depend on logger mode.
field_notes.columns: Result values from the scheduled SQL; values are commonly strings.
